claim: This 2018 review supports a field-map taxonomy in which force/torque-based impedance and position/velocity-based admittance are distinct causal realizations, extended by explicit force tracking, variable impedance and flexible-joint SEA/VSA actuation. Coupled stability and transparency are architecture-dependent properties shaped by sensing, backdrivability, inner-loop bandwidth, friction, environment stiffness and gain variation. It is decision-grade only for taxonomy, mechanism lineage and gap identification, not primary comparative, performance or safety evidence.
claim_locator: Impedance/admittance realization, force tracking, variable-impedance passivity, SEA/VSA and conclusion.
epistemic_status: review-level technical narrative for taxonomy, mechanism lineage and gap identification only
problem_and_setting: Organizing active impedance control for rigid and compliant robots, indirect/explicit force regulation, variable gains and nested loops under uncertain contact.
method_or_mechanism: Distinguishes force/torque impedance from position/velocity admittance; reviews force compensators modifying reference or stiffness. Time-varying stiffness can inject energy; remedies include damping coordination, energy tanks, constrained adaptation and state-independent schedules. SEA/VSA adds compliant transmissions and nested loops.
content_summary: Position-based outer filters regulate force indirectly and can retain steady error under unknown environment stiffness/location. A stiffness-rate term in storage derivative means arbitrary stiffness increases can violate passivity. SEA improves shock tolerance/backdrivability/torque sensing but adds bandwidth, vibration, drift, delay and nested-loop tradeoffs. Gaps include VIC-force tracking links, time-varying stability and flexible-joint impedance.
synthesis_role: Supports Active Field Map categories of causal realization, explicit force tracking, passivity-aware VIC and compliant actuation.
development_link: Connects fixed-gain causality to passivity-aware VIC and SEA/VSA hardware-aware implementation.

evidence.finding: Force/torque impedance and position/velocity admittance are distinct realizations with architecture-dependent transparency and stability.
Unknown environment properties create steady force error; compensation modifies reference, stiffness or both.
The stiffness-rate term can inject energy and break passivity.
Damping coordination, energy tanks, constrained adaptation and state-independent schedules limit or account for gain energy.
Compliant actuation improves impact/backdrivability/torque sensing but adds bandwidth, vibration, drift, noise, delay and passivity constraints.
Open gaps concern VIC-force tracking, time-varying stability and flexible-joint control.

boundary_conditions: Decision-grade is restricted to field classification and lineage.
No primary comparative or safety evidence is supplied.
Many arguments use simplified linear outer loops and passive environments.
assumptions: Environment and inner loops fit reviewed models.
Sensing, friction, delay and actuators remain in assumed regimes.
Energy accounting and storage functions are correct.
The taxonomy is descriptive, not exhaustive.

reported: Indirect force regulation can retain steady error.
Unconstrained stiffness increase can break passivity.
SEA may lose bandwidth or exhibit vibration, drift, noise and instability.
inferred: Narrative selection bias cannot be excluded.
Heterogeneous evidence cannot establish ranking or general safety.
Taxonomic boundaries can overlap in hybrid implementations.

verification_status: verified against Controller-supplied admitted full text
